trust_decision.summary: The TLS/DTLS 1.2 record layer decides whether an unauthenticated incoming AEAD record is long enough to process. At the pinned commit it passes undersized records to the cipher's TLS1_AAD ctrl. The provider rejects them there, and tls1_cipher then turns that rejection into an RLAYERfatal internal_error. So DTLS tears down the connection when it should silently drop the record.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'DTLS 1.2 AEAD record', so an engineer starts at dtls_process_record's cipher call and its silent-drop branch. From there they follow funcs->cipher into tls1_cipher's AEAD AAD block, ssl/record/methods/tls1_meth.c:291-296.

fix_sites.entry_point: SSL_read_ex / SSL_read / SSL_do_handshake on a DTLS 1.2 or TLS 1.2 connection with an AEAD suite (GCM, CCM, CCM8, ChaCha20-Poly1305), via dtls_process_record (ssl/record/methods/dtls_meth.c:190) or tls_get_more_records (ssl/record/methods/tls_common.c:773)
fix_sites.module_kind: core record layer (shared TLS/DTLS 1.2 record method, ssl/record/methods)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The DTLS encrypt-then-MAC path is not an AEAD cipher, and the advisory title says 'AEAD record'. Its fatal length and MAC checks also look like long-standing, deliberate upstream behaviour.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: After a forged short record is dropped, a valid DTLS record with the same sequence number must still be accepted, so the replay bitmap must not be advanced for the dropped record. TLS (non-DTLS) must still send a fatal bad_record_mac alert. A fix that makes the failure non-fatal for TLS too, or that marks the forged record as received, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: AES-GCM record shorter than explicit IV (8) + tag (16)
AES-CCM record shorter than 8 + 16, including a zero-length record
ChaCha20-Poly1305 record shorter than 16 (no explicit IV)
the same check on TLS 1.2, where the alert must be bad_record_mac rather than internal_error

O7_producer.where: rl->eivlen and rl->taglen are set when the record layer is created (ssl/record/methods/tls1_meth.c:158-164, ssl/record/methods/tls_common.c:1277); this is key setup, not a schema or serializer producer

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DTLS encrypt-then-MAC path: an unauthenticated record shorter than the MAC, or with a bad MAC, calls RLAYERfatal (decode_error / bad_record_mac) instead of silently dropping the record, which kills the DTLS connection
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: This is CBC+ETM, not AEAD, and the advisory names AEAD; the TLS path at ssl/record/methods/tls_common.c:744-755 is fatal by design
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point, about 25 lines above the cipher call

O8b_injection_room.sibling: the TLS 1.3 record method already checks rec->length < rl->taglen + 1 before AEAD; removing it in our copy would give a second-implementation sibling (a separate record method in another file)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Each record method keeps its own length checks; a maintainer refactoring tls13_cipher could plausibly drop it, assuming the provider rejects short input

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a planted DTLS pre-cipher minimum-length check that only counts the tag and forgets eivlen (or the reverse), so CCM8 or GCM records between the two bounds still reach the fatal AAD ctrl
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: dtls_get_max_record_overhead (ssl/record/methods/dtls_meth.c:713) already adds up eivlen + taglen, so a partial copy of that arithmetic is a natural mistake

O9_family: CWE-1284 improper validation of specified quantity (record length vs. mandatory AEAD overhead); its effect is unauthenticated DTLS connection termination

O10_build.project_tests: test/recordlentest.c (test/recipes/70-test_recordlen.t) is the file the fix extends; test/dtlstest.c and test/sslapitest.c also cover DTLS. The tests use in-memory BIOs from test/helpers/ssltestlib.c, so no network is needed

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: In dtls_process_record, treat any enc_err==0 as a silent drop (ignore rl->alert), or stop RLAYERfatal on pad<=0 in tls1_cipher for every case. Either one masks real internal errors or removes the TLS bad_record_mac alert, instead of rejecting short records before the AAD ctrl.

out_of_scope_notes: In DTLS, records that fail decompression or exceed max_frag_len are also fatal (ssl/record/methods/dtls_meth.c:239-258), but these checks run after authentication, so they are outside the unauthenticated-record scope.
The stitched AES-CBC-HMAC ciphers also take the AEAD-flag branch, but ssl/ssl_ciph.c:507-510 enables them only for TLS (major version 3), not DTLS.
unverified: present_in_latest is unknown because no latest release was given.

Whether upstream treats the DTLS ETM fatal paths (ssl/record/methods/dtls_meth.c:165-176) as intended or as a bug is not established. A hidden test for that route would assert behaviour beyond the published fix.
Of the 9 fix commits, 5 are release-prep commits (version/CHANGES only) and 4 are identical backports of the same one-hunk change. The real source change is a single site.
The legacy (non-provider) EVP AEAD ctrl path in crypto/evp/e_aes.c was not traced. The fix's check runs before the ctrl, so it would cover that path too.
